question: Suppose a doctor has prescribed a corrective lens of power +2.5 D. The focal length of the lens is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**+40 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power of a lens (P) is the reciprocal of its focal length (f) in meters, given by the formula P=(1)/(f)
 
• For a lens with Power +2.5D, f=(1)/(2.5)m,
 
• Calculating f , we get f=0.4m.
 
• To convert the focal length from meters to centimeters, multiply by 100.
 
• Thus, f=0.4×100=40cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diopters (D)**

 
 
• Diopter is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens.
 
• It is the reciprocal of the focal length measured in meters (1/m).
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f)**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance between the lens and the point where it converges or diverges light.
 
• It is measured in meters or centimeters depending on the context.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens**
 
 
• A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges and converges light rays to a focal point.
 
• It has a positive focal length and power.
 
 
 
• **Optical Power**
 
 
• Optical power of a lens determines how strongly it converges or diverges light.
 
• It is crucial in designing glasses, microscopes, and cameras.
